title: Rehearse a short research presentation
objective: Give a complete short talk, use feedback, and improve one part.

slides.title: Plan six short notes
body: Question. Method. Result. Meaning. Limit. Next step.
Give most of your time to the result and its meaning. Use notes you can look at quickly.

slides.title: Listen for evidence and a limit
body: “We asked where snails were seen. We counted for ten minutes at two sites.”
“We saw 5 snails by a tree and 2 by a wall. The tree count was higher on that visit.”
“We only visited once. We want to count on more days.”

slides.title: Read the first case together
body: Rehearsal notes: A class asked when frogs were seen at a pond. In equal periods it saw 3 in the morning and 7 at dusk. There was one visit per period.

slides.title: Try it with a partner
body: Give a short talk with the question, the two counts and one limit.
Answer two audience questions: Which time had more? Would another day give the same result?
Use three notes: question, result, limit.

slides.title: Try a new case
body: Rehearsal notes: A class asked when birds were seen in a garden. In equal periods it saw 8 in the morning and 4 at dusk. There was one visit per period.

slides.title: Work on your own
body: Give a short talk with the question, the two counts and one limit.
Answer two audience questions: Which time had more? Would another day give the same result?
Ask for feedback. Name one change you will make for your next talk.

slides.title: Repeat your weakest part
body: Your partner names one clear point and asks one question. Use that feedback to deliver the difficult part again.
